subject: Cooking
title: How Water Temperature Changes Everything
description: A micro-lesson that makes How Water Temperature Changes Everything usable.

hook.text: Boiling water ruins green tea but is perfect for black tea. The difference is just 25°F — and it matters enormously.

buildup.text: Water temperature controls which compounds are extracted from tea leaves and coffee grounds.

discovery.text: Green tea brewed at 175°F releases sweet amino acids. At 212°F, bitter tannins dominate and destroy delicacy.

twist.text: Coffee's ideal extraction temperature is 195–205°F — too hot burns it, too cold under-extracts.

climax.text: Japanese gyokuro tea is brewed at just 140°F — producing an intensely sweet, umami-rich liquor.

punchline.text: The difference between good tea and bad tea is often just a thermometer.

quiz.question: Why should green tea not be brewed with boiling water?
options: Boiling water extracts bitter tannins that overwhelm delicate flavors

details.summary: Water temperature dramatically affects extraction of coffee and tea compounds. Hotter water extracts faster but pulls bitter compounds. Green tea brewed at 175°F is sweet and vegetal; at 212°F it becomes harsh and bitter.
details.whyItMatters: Temperature control is the single most impactful variable most home brewers ignore. A simple thermometer can transform the taste of both tea and coffee immediately.
takeaways: Green tea needs 160 to 175°F to avoid bitter tannin extraction
Coffee extracts best at 195 to 205°F for balanced flavor
Hotter water extracts more compounds faster, including undesirable ones

faq.question: Why does green tea taste bitter when brewed with boiling water?
faq.answer: Boiling water rapidly extracts catechins and tannins from green tea leaves, producing harsh bitterness. At 160 to 175°F, amino acids like L-theanine extract first, contributing sweetness and umami before excessive catechins are pulled. Temperature controls which compounds dominate.

faq.question: What temperature should different teas be brewed at?
faq.answer: White tea: 160 to 185°F for delicate sweetness. Green tea: 160 to 175°F to preserve freshness. Oolong: 185 to 205°F depending on oxidation level. Black tea: 200 to 212°F for full body and malt. Pu-erh: full boiling at 212°F. Each tea's oxidation level determines its ideal extraction temperature.
